turn_prompts: Start a new fenced authoring conversation, read validation_repair_context first, then read the prior candidate snapshot, validation_receipt, verification_contract, and any critic findings. Critic findings are optional; validation_repair_context is the primary diagnosis. Write only the fixed candidate files. Each repair turn has exactly one candidate-validation opportunity: call harbor_validate_candidate at most once in this turn. A rejected receipt ends this turn; do not call the tool again until the next prompt. When provisioning Debian packages in environment/Dockerfile, switch the default Debian APT sources from HTTP to HTTPS before apt-get update; the controlled build network permits HTTPS egress only. When the frozen VerificationContract invokes test.sh through sh, both test.sh and solution/solve.sh must be POSIX sh compatible: do not use set -o pipefail, bash arrays, [[, or other Bash-only syntax.

Read validation_repair_context before critic findings; critic findings are optional context only. Correct the documented failing layer in the candidate workspace, then call harbor_validate_candidate once to create the next immutable snapshot and receipt.

If validation remains rejected, compare validation_repair_context, the current candidate, the frozen VerificationContract, baseline behavior, and Oracle behavior. Apply one focused correction and call harbor_validate_candidate once; do not alter frozen source inputs or the verifier contract.

Use validation_repair_context to repair the narrow failing layer: layout, environment provisioning, baseline, Oracle, coverage, or integrity. Keep scripts POSIX sh when the contract invokes them through sh, then validate the replacement candidate once.

Re-read validation_repair_context and the most recent receipt before changing files. Preserve every successful constraint while correcting only the remaining failure, and call harbor_validate_candidate once after the repair.

Continue the bounded repair loop from the latest immutable candidate and validation_repair_context. Do not hide failures, bypass the verifier, or substitute a different repository, command, or source revision; validate the next focused correction once.

Before another validation, check that instruction, task metadata, environment, solution, test script, and tests analysis agree with the frozen task and verification contracts, using validation_repair_context as the failure map. Submit the repaired candidate through one harbor_validate_candidate call.

Use the final available repair turn only for a correction supported by validation_repair_context and the latest receipt. Call harbor_validate_candidate once and rely on its immutable receipt; a passing receipt ends the repair loop.
